artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

Split Enz.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
Split Enz's True Colours is a landmark rock album released in 1980, marking a pivotal moment in the band's career. Originally issued by Mushroom Records and later associated with Warner Music, the album blends new wave, pop, and art rock influences, showcasing the group's inventive songwriting and distinctive sound. With its crisp production and melodic hooks, True Colours stands out for its polished arrangements and the increased creative presence of Neil Finn, who contributed more prominently as both a vocalist and songwriter compared to earlier releases.

Musically, the album is defined by its energetic rhythms, layered harmonies, and quirky instrumentation, reflecting Split Enz's unique approach to rock. Tracks like "I Got You" and "I Hope I Never" became signature songs, highlighting the band's ability to merge catchy pop sensibilities with artful experimentation. True Colours was the band's first major commercial breakthrough, reaching high chart positions in Australia and New Zealand and gaining international attention. Critically, it was praised for its originality and craftsmanship, cementing Split Enz's reputation as one of the most innovative rock acts of the era and setting the stage for their continued success throughout the early 1980s.
